# FastPubSub Rust SDK

> Rust client library for FastPubSubNetwork contract v0.1 — realtime publish/subscribe over WebSocket.

Crate: [fastpubsub-sdk on crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/fastpubsub-sdk)
Repository: [github.com/fastpubsub/rust-sdk](https://github.com/fastpubsub/rust-sdk)
Full guide: [README.md](README.md)
Developer docs: [doc.fastpubsub.com](https://doc.fastpubsub.com)
Product context: [fastpubsub.com/llms.txt](https://www.fastpubsub.com/llms.txt)

## What This SDK Is For

Use this crate when a Rust service, worker, or desktop tool needs to:

- connect to a FastPubSub edge over WebSocket;
- create, refresh, and revoke short-lived access tokens from a master token;
- publish binary payloads to `tenant + channel`;
- subscribe to channel patterns like `public.#`;
- apply route filters (compression, encryption, fragmentation, batching, delta, latest-only, send-rate, bandwidth).

This SDK talks to the managed FastPubSub network. It is not a self-hosted broker client.

## What This SDK Is Not

- Not a durable queue, stream processor, or Kafka/NATS/RabbitMQ replacement.
- Not for message replay, consumer groups, or guaranteed persistence.
- WebTransport API exists but the network task is still a stub in v0.1.
- `publish` success means local SDK/transport acceptance, not confirmed delivery to every remote subscriber.

## Key Concepts

| Term | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `overlay` | Environment name, e.g. `globaltest` for dev/test |
| `tenant` | Namespace inside an access token; rights are per tenant |
| `channel` | Concrete publish route, e.g. `public.chat.room1` — no wildcards in publish |
| `channel_pattern` | Subscription pattern, e.g. `public.#` |
| `payload` | Binary data; SDK does not force JSON or protobuf |
| `SdkMessage` | What subscribers receive after inbound filters |

## Recommended Flow

```text
open(overlay)
  -> resolve_edge()
  -> create_access_token()
  -> session.web_socket(access_token)?.build().await?
  -> publish / subscribe
```

`resolve_edge()` discovers bootstrap candidates, probes `GET {api_base}/ping` in parallel, and selects the fastest edge.

## Cargo Dependency

```toml
[dependencies]
fastpubsub_sdk = { package = "fastpubsub-sdk", version = "0.3" }
```

Import path is `fastpubsub_sdk` (crate renamed in `Cargo.toml`).

Default features: `rest`, `websocket`, `access_token_json`, `debug_log_format_json`.

Transport only:

```toml
fastpubsub_sdk = { package = "fastpubsub-sdk", version = "0.3", default-features = false, features = ["websocket"] }
```

## Minimal Example

```rust
use fastpubsub_sdk::client::{open, FastPubSub};
use fastpubsub_sdk::transport::{SubscribeOptions, WebSocketTransport};
use fastpubsub_sdk::{CreateAccessTokenBuilder, TenantGrant};

let mut session = open("globaltest");
session.resolve_edge().await?;

let access_token = CreateAccessTokenBuilder::new()
    .created_by("my-app")
    .expires_at_input("+1h")?
    .tenant_grant(
        TenantGrant::new(vec!["tenant_1".to_string()])
            .allow_pub(vec!["public.#".to_string()])
            .allow_sub(vec!["public.#".to_string()]),
    )
    .create_with_config(session.api_base()?, &master_token, session.http_config())
    .await?;

let mut client: FastPubSub<WebSocketTransport> =
    session.web_socket(access_token)?.build().await?;

let mut rx = client
    .subscribe("tenant_1", "public.#", &SubscribeOptions::default())
    .await?;

client.publish("tenant_1", "public.demo", b"hello").await?;
```

Runnable examples: `examples/websocket.rs`, `examples/latest_receiver.rs`, `examples/latest_state_sync.rs`, `examples/chat_broadcast.rs`.

## Publish Delivery Modes

Use `publish_with_options` for explicit delivery:

| `PublishDeliveryMode` | Wire | Behaviour |
|-----------------------|------|-----------|
| `Broadcast` | v1 frame | All overlay nodes and all local subscribers |
| `DeliverOneLowLatency` | v2, mode `1` | One lowest-latency overlay node; one random local subscriber on edge |
| `DeliverOneRandom` | v2, mode `2` | One random overlay node; one random local subscriber |

`publish()` without options sends broadcast (legacy v1 frame). Deliver-one modes do nothing when no subscribers exist.

## Filters — Rules For Users And AI

- Register the same filter list on sender and receiver for the same `tenant + channel` prefix.
- Inbound filters run in registration order; outbound filters run in reverse order.
- Use wider prefixes only when all child channels need the same filter, e.g. `public.` covers `public.chat` and `public.state`.
- Timer-based filters need `filter_timer_mode` on the builder.

Available filters: `CompressedFilter`, `EncryptionFilter`, `FragmentFilter`, `ChannelBatchFilter`, `Delta16Filter`, `Delta32Filter`, `Delta64Filter`, `SendRateFilter`, `LatestOnlyFilter`, `BandwidthLimiterFilter`, `DebugLogFilter`, `DummyFilter`.

`FragmentFilter` subscriptions must include the main channel and control channel, e.g. `files.photo.#`.

## WS Link Quality

- HTTP `GET /ping` during `resolve_edge()` selects the edge.
- Optional application `PING`/`PONG` on the open WebSocket measures RTT (`ping_interval_secs(1|3|5)`, `link_quality()`, `RttMeasured` event).

## Environment Variables

| Variable | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `FPS_MASTER_TOKEN` | Master token for `/v1/get-token` |
| `FPS_ACCESS_TOKEN` | Access token for direct endpoint examples |
| `FPS_WS_ENDPOINT` | WebSocket endpoint for direct endpoint examples |
| `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` | Proxy URL |
| `FPS_EXTRA_CA_CERT` | Extra CA file paths, comma-separated |

## REST Helpers (before transport connect)

| Method | Path | Auth | Purpose |
|--------|------|------|---------|
| `GET` | `/ping` | none | Measure edge latency |
| `POST` | `/v1/get-token` | Bearer master token | Create access token |
| `PUT` | `/v1/refresh-token` | Bearer master token | Extend AT expiry |
| `DELETE` | `/v1/revoke-token` | Bearer master token | Revoke access token |

Helpers: `refresh_access_token`, `refresh_access_token_from_at`, `revoke_access_token`, `access_token_id`, `parse_access_token`.

## Limits In v0.1

- Publish frame v2 (`0x02` tag) encodes delivery mode; broadcast keeps legacy v1.
- WebTransport has no real network task yet.
- Delivery success is local SDK acceptance, not end-to-end confirmation.
